newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu to leave hospital Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu to leave hospital Thursday.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, facing a rapidly spreading rebellion in eastern Zaire, will leave hospital in Monaco on Thursday after follow-up treatment for prostate cancer, his spokesman said on Wednesday.
Airport officials in Nice said the 66-year-old president's private plane arrived on Tuesday night and was standing by to take him back to his war-torn country.
No date had been set yet for his departure and it was not clear whether he would go to Kinshasa or to a jungle palace in his home town of Gbadolite, more than 1,000 km (600 miles) from the capital.

Mobutu's planned release from the Princess Grace hospital and the plane's arrival were the clearest signs yet that the veteran strongman aims to return to Zaire and make a stand against rebels sweeping across the east of the country.
Aides said Mobutu would leave hospital at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT) and would hold a photo session at his French Riviera villa in a clear attempt to quell reports that he is seriously ill.
He was admitted to the Monaco clinic at the weekend after a month convalescing in his nearby Riviera mansion from prostate surgery in Switzerland last August.

Mobutu's son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga has repeatedly said that his father, in power for almost 32 years, aims to return soon to Zaire in a bid to rally ragged government troops against the mainly Tutsi rebels, led by Laurent Kabila.
Mobutu's white Boeing 727 and a cargo plane that transports his belongings were both waiting at the Riviera airport.
France expressed growing worry on Wednesday over events in Zaire, a former Belgian colony, and said it was taking measures to protect its citizens.
"The current uncertainties have led us to take the necessary measures concerning the security of our citizens," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a regular briefing.
"We are in close communication with our European and American partners," he added. He gave no further details.
Rummelhardt said the attempt on Tuesday by Zaire's parliamentary opposition to oust Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, was a particular concern.
Kengo is in Kenya where African leaders opened a meeting in Nairobi on Wednesday on the Zaire crisis with a strong call for negotiations to end the war tearing the country apart.
Mobutu has spent most of his time in Europe since his cancer surgery. His departure has repeatedly been announced as imminent by his entourage, only to be delayed for medical reasons.
The Congolese Red Cross said on Tuesday that members of Mobutu's family had taken refuge across the Zaire river in neighbouring Congo in the face of advances by the rebels.
